notes: Behaviour evals in skill-creator's schema. File paths are relative to the repository root. Expectations are checked against the transcript and the produced files; visual quality itself needs a human or blind-comparison review.

evals.name: landing-from-scratch
evals.prompt: Build a landing page for Spoke & Lantern, a volunteer bicycle repair co-op in Tbilisi. It only opens 18:00 to 23:00, has four repair stands, and prices are pay-what-you-can. Plain HTML/CSS is fine, put it in ./spoke-lantern/.
evals.expected_output: A complete, responsive landing page whose concept comes from the co-op's own facts (evening hours, four stands, pay-what-you-can), not from a startup template, verified in a browser.
expectations: States the mode as Create and the surface as Persuade (or equivalent wording)
Writes down the category rut (and its opposite) before choosing a direction
Considers at least three directions that differ on at least three axes, each tied to a different fact about the co-op
The chosen idea uses a subject-specific fact (hours, stands, or pay-what-you-can) as a visible device
Contains no invented testimonials, logos, ratings, member counts or press
Uses no remote placeholder image services (picsum, unsplash-source, placehold)
Every h1/h2 renders in two lines or fewer at 390px wide
Includes visible focus styles and a prefers-reduced-motion rule if anything moves
Rendered the page at phone and desktop widths and looked at the screenshots before reporting
The final report lists sample content that must be replaced and says which checks ran

evals.name: operate-dashboard
evals.prompt: Make the main dashboard for the front desk of a small veterinary clinic: today's appointments, who is waiting, overdue vaccinations, and quick check-in. Static HTML with fake but realistic sample data in ./vet-desk/.
evals.expected_output: A dense, scannable Operate screen whose hierarchy follows the receptionist's decisions, with complete states.
expectations: Identifies the surface as Operate and does not apply a marketing/landing-page lane
The top of the screen answers what needs attention now (waiting patients or the next appointment)
Check-in is reachable in one action from each appointment
Numbers in tables are right-aligned with tabular figures
Any KPI shown has a unit and a comparison or an action it informs; no decorative KPI tiles
Includes empty, loading or error states for at least the appointment list
Sample data is labelled as sample in the report
No staggered or scroll-reveal entrance animation on the working screen

evals.name: redesign-keep-identity
evals.prompt: This is our studio's homepage: evals/files/studio-landing.html. It feels weak and a bit broken on phones. Improve it, but it still has to feel like Tidewater.
evals.expected_output: An audit first, then a refined page that keeps the harbour blue, signal orange, circular stamp motif and Alegreya Sans, while fixing real defects.
expectations: Renders and audits the page before editing it
Writes an explicit preserve list naming the stamp/circle motif and the harbour blue + signal orange colours
Keeps Alegreya Sans and the two brand colours
Fixes the 112px no-wrap headline that overflows on phones
Raises the muted grey text (#9aa6ad on paper) to at least 4.5:1
Restores visible keyboard focus on links and the button (the original removes outlines)
Compares before and after screenshots at the same widths
Does not introduce a new typeface, palette or radius language

evals.name: modify-dropdown
evals.prompt: In evals/files/app-settings.html the Language dropdown has no hover or focus state and just pops open. Make it feel nicer.
evals.expected_output: A bounded change to the dropdown only, using the file's existing tokens, made keyboard-accessible with calm, short motion.
expectations: Treats the task as Modify and does not restyle other parts of the form
Reuses existing tokens (--accent, --line, --r, --t, --ease-out) rather than adding new colour or timing values
Makes the trigger a real button with aria-expanded and a visible focus-visible style
Menu supports keyboard use (arrow keys or tab to options, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger)
Open/close motion is 250ms or less, uses transform/opacity, and has a reduced-motion path
Reports what changed and how it was checked in one or two lines

evals.name: audit-generic-ai-page
evals.prompt: Why does evals/files/generic-landing.html feel so AI-generated? Don't change anything, just tell me.
evals.expected_output: A read-only audit with a decision trace, a root-cause cluster and verdicts whose replacements are not new clichés.
expectations: Does not modify the file
Includes a decision trace: visible elements and whether each has a reason to exist
Flags 'trusted by 10,000+ teams' as an unsupported claim (truth), separate from taste
Groups the gradient/glow/glass/shadow effects into one root-cause finding instead of listing them as unrelated tweaks
Does not recommend replacing the look with a cream background, serif display and terracotta accent
Notes at least one item to keep or question rather than condemning every pattern
Says whether the page was rendered or only read

evals.name: experimental-experience
evals.prompt: Make an experimental one-page portfolio for Aru Sadyk, a sound artist who records ice cracking on Lake Baikal in winter. Go wild, I want it to feel like nothing else. ./aru/
evals.expected_output: An Experience surface whose concept comes from the artist's material, ambitious but still usable.
expectations: Identifies the surface as Experience
The concept is derived from the subject (ice, cracking, sound, Baikal), not from a generic dark portfolio template
The artist's name, a list of works and a contact method are visible and keyboard-reachable
Any canvas/WebGL/audio interaction has a reduced-motion or no-script fallback
Audio never autoplays without a user action
Rendered and looked at the result before reporting

evals.name: responsive-verification
evals.prompt: Check evals/files/generic-landing.html on mobile and desktop and tell me what breaks.
evals.expected_output: A rendered check at real widths with evidence, honest about what was not tested.
expectations: Renders at a phone width (≈390px) and a desktop width (≈1440px)
Reports the hero headline wrapping to many lines at phone width
Reports the low-contrast muted text
Labels each finding as verified (rendered) or code-read
Does not claim Safari or other browsers were tested if they were not
Does not edit the file

evals.name: continuous-qa-new-field
evals.prompt: Add a phone number field to the settings form in evals/files/app-settings.html.
evals.expected_output: A new field that matches the existing field pattern exactly, with correct semantics, and nothing else changed.
expectations: The new field reuses the existing .field / label / input / .help pattern
Uses type="tel" and autocomplete="tel" with a visible label
No new colours, sizes or radius values are introduced
Does not redesign or restyle unrelated parts of the form

evals.name: user-pins-a-cliche
evals.prompt: Landing page for Ledgerly, our invoicing tool for freelancers. I want Inter everywhere and a purple-to-blue gradient hero, that's our brand. ./ledgerly/
evals.expected_output: The user's pinned font and gradient are honoured and executed well; Lagann does not overrule tier-1 requirements with its anti-slop signals.
expectations: Uses Inter as the typeface
Uses a purple-to-blue gradient in the hero
Does not lecture the user or replace the requested gradient with a flat colour
Text on the gradient passes contrast (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text)
Brings specificity elsewhere (copy, proof, the product's own invoice UI) rather than generic feature cards
Contains no invented customer logos, testimonials or usage numbers
